title: Transpose formula for a general mate square
statement:
For adjunctions L1⊣R1 and L2⊣R2, functors G,H, and a right square τ:R1⋅G→H⋅R2, let α:G⋅L2→L1⋅H be its left mate. For every P,M and f:L1(P)→M, the L2⊣R2 transpose of α(P) followed by H(f) is G of the L1⊣R1 transpose of f, followed by τ(M).

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe a av b bv c cv d dv
variable {A : Type a} [Category.{av} A] {B : Type b} [Category.{bv} B]
  {C : Type c} [Category.{cv} C] {D : Type d} [Category.{dv} D]
  {L₁ : A ⥤ B} {R₁ : B ⥤ A} {L₂ : C ⥤ D} {R₂ : D ⥤ C}
  {G : A ⥤ C} {H : B ⥤ D}
theorem adjunctionMate_transpose (a₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁) (a₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂)
    (τ : TwoSquare R₁ H G R₂) (P : A) (M : B) (f : L₁.obj P ⟶ M) :
    a₂.homEquiv (G.obj P) (H.obj M)
      (((mateEquiv a₁ a₂).symm τ).app P ≫ H.map f) =
    G.map (a₁.homEquiv P M f) ≫ τ.app M
```

proof.text: Expand the mate at the first adjunction unit, then use naturality in the target of the second Hom equivalence. The unit-mate identity and naturality of τ replace the composite by G applied to the first unit followed by R1(f), which is exactly the first transpose.
